examples.en: The number of infected people is rising fast.
Infected people need to rest at home.
The health center treats infected people separately.
I have never met an infected person.
The number of infected people dropped from yesterday.
News about infected people is on the news.

explain: '감염자'는 뉴스나 보건 기사에서 자주 쓰는 말이고, 병원에서 몸이 아픈 사람은 '환자'라고 해요. 증상이 없어도 병균이 몸에 있으면 감염자예요. '확진자'는 검사로 확인된 사람이라서 조금 달라요.
explain_en: 감염자 is common in news and health reports, while a person who is sick at a hospital is a 환자. Someone can be a 감염자 even without symptoms. 확진자 means a person confirmed by a test, so it is slightly different.

en: pedagogy; education (as a field of study)

examples.en: I study education at university.
I have an education class this afternoon.
My sister majored in education.
Education textbooks are not as hard as I thought.
To become a teacher, you need to know education theory too.
That person is a professor of education.

explain: '교육'은 가르치고 배우는 일이고, 교육학은 그것을 연구하는 학문 이름이에요. 대학에는 '교육학과'가 있고, 교사가 되려는 사람이 많이 공부해요. '경제학', '심리학'처럼 '-학'이 붙은 말과 함께 묶어서 외우면 쉬워요.
explain_en: '교육' is the act of teaching and learning, while 교육학 is the name of the academic field that studies it. Universities have a '교육학과' (department of education), and many people who want to become teachers study it. It is easy to remember together with other '-학' words like '경제학' and '심리학'.

examples.en: This film won the grand prize at the film festival.
The grand prize goes to the best work.
Our school band won the grand prize.
Who is this year's grand prize winner?
I will practice hard aiming for the grand prize.
I watched the car racing grand prix on TV.

explain: '대상'과 거의 같은 뜻이지만, 대상은 학교 행사·방송·공모전에서 더 흔하고 그랑프리는 영화제·광고제·디자인 상처럼 외국 대회 이름을 따라 쓸 때 많이 들어요. 'F1 그랑프리'처럼 자동차 경주 대회 이름이기도 해요. '그랑프리를 받다', '그랑프리를 타다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '대상', but 대상 is more common for school events, TV shows and contests, while 그랑프리 is often heard for film festivals, ad festivals and design awards that follow foreign naming. It is also the name of car races, as in 'F1 그랑프리'. People say '그랑프리를 받다' or '그랑프리를 타다'.

en: slightly more than; a little over

examples.en: It is a little over an hour from home to school.

examples.ko: 그 일은 한 달 남짓한 시간이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: The work took a little over a month.
A man just over 170 centimeters tall came.
A little over ten friends gathered.
You will arrive in a little over thirty minutes.
I lived here for a little over five years.

explain: '남짓하다'는 수나 양 뒤에 붙어서 '그것보다 조금 더 많다'고 말해요. 보통 '한 시간 남짓', '열 명 남짓'처럼 숫자 바로 뒤에 써요. '정도'는 많거나 적을 수 있지만 '남짓'은 조금 넘는 쪽이에요.
explain_en: 남짓하다 comes right after a number or amount and means a bit more than it, as in 한 시간 남짓 or 열 명 남짓. 정도 can be a bit more or a bit less, but 남짓 only leans slightly over.

examples.en: A welcome rain finally fell after a long time.
The farmers waited for the welcome rain.
Thanks to the rain, the fields came back to life.
The rain that fell last night was really welcome.
The news reported rain coming tomorrow.
The trees turned green with the rain.

explain: 그냥 '비'가 아니라 오래 가물 때 내리는 반가운 비를 '단비'라고 해요. 비가 오면 불편한 사람도 많아서, 기다리던 비일 때만 이 말을 써요. '단'은 '달다'와 같은 뜻이라서 비가 달게 느껴진다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 바쁠 때 친구가 도와줘서 가뭄에 단비 같았어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꼭 필요한 때에 받은 도움이나 좋은 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes help or good news that arrives exactly when it is badly needed.

explain_en: 단비 is the welcome rain that falls after a long dry spell. It is only used when people were waiting for the rain. The 단 is the same as in 달다 (sweet), so the rain feels sweet.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 당뇨가 있어서 단 음식을 조심해요.
examples.en: My grandfather has diabetes, so he is careful with sweet food.
Steady management is important for diabetes.
I also had a diabetes test at my health checkup.
My father takes diabetes medicine every day.
I started exercising to prevent diabetes.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 당뇨 때문에 설탕을 줄이라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor told me to cut down on sugar because of diabetes.

explain: 병원에서는 '당뇨병'이라고 하고, 일상에서는 줄여서 '당뇨'라고 많이 해요. '당뇨가 있다'라고 말하고, 병에 걸렸다고 할 때는 '당뇨병에 걸리다'가 자연스러워요. 피 속의 당은 '혈당'이라고 해요.
explain_en: At the hospital the full word is 당뇨병, but in daily life people shorten it to 당뇨. You say 당뇨가 있다, and for catching the disease the natural phrase is 당뇨병에 걸리다. Sugar in the blood is called 혈당.

examples.en: Our company landed a big contract.
The athlete was happy to win the gold medal.

examples.ko: 그는 어려운 경쟁 끝에 일자리를 따냈어요.
examples.en: After tough competition, he got the job.

examples.ko: 내년에는 더 많은 주문을 따낼 거예요.
examples.en: Next year we will win more orders.
The team stayed up all night to win the construction job.
I envy my friend who landed a good position.

explain: '따내다'는 경쟁해서 계약, 메달, 일 같은 것을 얻어 낼 때 써요. 그냥 '받다'와 달리 힘들게 경쟁한 느낌이 있어요. 점수를 얻을 때는 '따다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: 따내다 is used when you win something like a contract, medal, or job through competition. Unlike plain 받다, it carries the feeling of a hard fight. For scores or grades, people more often say 따다.

examples.ko: 들판에 백마 한 마리가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A white horse stands in the field.

examples.ko: 동화 속 왕자는 백마를 타고 와요.
examples.en: The prince in fairy tales comes riding a white horse.
A white horse has fur as white as snow.
The child drew a picture of a white horse.
I once saw a white horse on Jeju Island.
That white horse is the one my uncle raises.

explain: 일상에서는 '하얀 말'이라고 하고, '백마'는 이야기나 글에서 더 자주 보여요. 동화 속 왕자는 보통 백마를 타요. '백'은 하얗다는 뜻의 한자어예요.

phrases.example: 백마 탄 왕자님을 기다리지 말고 스스로 길을 찾아요.
phrases.en: prince on a white horse; Prince Charming
phrases.nuance_ko: 이상형이나 나를 구해 줄 완벽한 사람을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an ideal partner or a perfect person who will come to rescue you.

explain_en: In daily talk people say 하얀 말, while 백마 appears more in stories and writing. A prince in a fairy tale usually rides a 백마. The 백 part is a Sino-Korean element meaning white.

examples.en: My dream is to be a translator who translates books.
The translator rendered the novel into Korean.
A famous translator translated this book.
I met a translator and heard their story.

examples.ko: 좋은 번역가가 되려면 두 언어를 잘 알아야 해요.
examples.en: To be a good translator you must know both languages well.
I gave a dictionary to my translator friend.

explain: '번역가'는 글을 번역하는 사람이고, 말로 바로 옮기는 사람은 '통역사'라고 해요. 책이나 영화 자막을 번역하는 사람은 번역가라고 해요. 직업을 말할 때는 '번역가예요'라고 해요.
explain_en: 번역가 is a person who translates written text, while someone who interprets speech on the spot is a 통역사. People who translate books or film subtitles are called 번역가. When stating a job, you say 번역가예요.

examples.en: The analyst looked through the market data.
I work as an analyst who studies data.
The soccer analyst explained the match in detail.

examples.ko: 분석가의 말에 따르면 내년에는 값이 오를 거예요.
examples.en: According to the analyst, prices will go up next year.
The company plans to hire a new analyst.

examples.ko: 뉴스에 나온 분석가가 이유를 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The analyst on the news explained the reason.

explain: '분석가'는 자료나 상황을 자세히 살펴서 결과를 설명하는 사람이에요. 뉴스에서 전문가가 나올 때 '경제 분석가', '축구 분석가'처럼 앞에 분야를 붙여요. 연구하는 사람은 '연구원'이라고 해서 조금 달라요.
explain_en: 분석가 is a person who examines data or situations closely and explains the result. On the news you will hear the field in front, like 경제 분석가 or 축구 분석가. A person who does research is a 연구원, which is a little different.

examples.ko: 그 영화의 속편이 다음 달에 나와요.
examples.en: The sequel to that film comes out next month.
I think the sequel is more fun.
The author is writing a sequel to the novel.

examples.ko: 속편을 보기 전에 앞 이야기를 다시 봤어요.
examples.en: I rewatched the first story before seeing the sequel.
Fans were happy about news of the drama sequel.
The sequel was not as fun as I expected.

explain: '속편'은 앞 이야기가 끝난 뒤의 이야기예요. 영화나 소설에 자주 쓰고, 드라마나 만화는 '2기', '시즌 2'라고 많이 말해요. 반대로 앞 이야기는 '전편'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 속편 is the story that continues after the first one ends. It is common for films and novels, while for dramas and cartoons people more often say 2기 or 시즌 2. The opposite, the earlier story, is 전편.

examples.en: Grandmother is carrying vegetables on a cart.
The man pulled a cart to the market.
In the old days people carried loads by cart.
It rained, and the cart got stuck in the mud.
The kids rode on the cart and played.
I have a lot of stuff, so I need a cart.

explain: '수레'는 바퀴가 달려서 짐을 싣고 끄는 도구예요. 지금은 시장이나 공사장에서 볼 수 있어요. 마트에서 쓰는 것은 '카트', 손으로 미는 작은 것은 '손수레'라고 해요.
explain_en: 수레 is a wheeled tool for loading and pulling goods. Today you mostly see it at markets or construction sites. The one used in a supermarket is a 카트, and a small hand-pushed one is a 손수레.

examples.en: The baby's breathing seems calm.
On winter mornings your breath looks white.
In the quiet room, only his breathing could be heard.
I felt a soft breath like a spring breeze.
She steadied her breath and began to sing.

examples.ko: 이 오래된 집에는 역사의 숨결이 남아 있어요.
examples.en: The breath of history remains in this old house.

explain: '숨결'은 숨을 쉬는 모양이나 느낌이에요. 일상에서 숨 쉬는 것 자체는 '숨'이라고 하고, '숨결'은 글이나 노래에서 부드럽게 표현할 때 더 많이 써요. '역사의 숨결'처럼 어떤 분위기가 느껴진다는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: 숨결 is how breathing looks or feels. Everyday breathing itself is just 숨, while 숨결 is used more in writing and songs for a soft feeling. It can also mean a sense of atmosphere, as in 역사의 숨결.

examples.en: You must not abuse people's trust.
Someone misused my photo.

examples.ko: 회사는 개인 정보가 악용되지 않게 조심해요.
examples.en: The company is careful so personal data is not misused.
Even good technology is dangerous when misused.

examples.ko: 그는 친구의 친절을 악용해서 돈을 빌렸어요.
examples.en: He took advantage of his friend's kindness to borrow money.
People who exploit the rules are the problem.

explain: '악용하다'는 좋은 목적으로 만든 것을 나쁜 일에 쓸 때 말해요. 비슷한 '이용하다'는 나쁜 뜻이 없지만, '악용하다'는 항상 나쁜 쓰임이에요. 반대로 좋은 곳에 쓰는 것은 '선용하다'라고 하는데 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: 악용하다 is used when something made for a good purpose is used for something bad. 이용하다 has no bad sense, but 악용하다 is always negative. The opposite, 선용하다, exists but is rarely used.

en: yahoo; woo-hoo (a cheer, or a shout on a mountain)

examples.en: At the top of the mountain I shouted "yahoo" loudly.
Yay! It's finally vacation!

examples.ko: 아이들은 눈을 보고 야호 하며 뛰어나갔어요.
examples.en: Seeing the snow, the kids ran out cheering.
The exam was over, so everyone cheered.
The shout echoed in the mountains.

examples.ko: 동생이 선물을 받고 야호 하고 좋아했어요.
examples.en: My little brother got a gift and cheered happily.

explain: '야호'는 기쁠 때 내는 소리이고, 특히 등산하다가 산 위에서 외치는 소리로 유명해요. 요즘은 산에서 소리를 지르는 것을 조심하라고 해서 예전만큼 많이 하지는 않아요. 기뻐서 외칠 때는 '앗싸'나 '만세'도 써요.
explain_en: 야호 is a sound of joy, and it is especially famous as the shout from a mountaintop while hiking. Today people are asked not to shout in the mountains, so it is done less than before. For a joyful cheer you can also say 앗싸 or 만세.

examples.en: I pay rent by automatic transfer.
How much is the transfer fee?

examples.ko: 이체가 아직 안 된 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems the transfer hasn't gone through yet.
Making a transfer with the app is convenient.
I went over today's transfer limit.

examples.ko: 이체 내역은 앱에서 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see your transfer history in the app.

explain: '이체'는 은행 계좌에서 다른 계좌로 돈을 보내는 것이에요. 말할 때는 보통 '송금'이나 '입금'을 더 많이 쓰고, '이체'는 은행 앱이나 '자동 이체'처럼 은행 용어로 자주 보여요. 다른 사람에게 돈을 보내면 송금, 받는 쪽에서 돈이 들어오면 입금이에요.
explain_en: 이체 means moving money from one bank account to another. In conversation people more often say 송금 or 입금, while 이체 shows up in bank apps and in 자동 이체. Sending money to someone is 송금, and money arriving on the receiving side is 입금.

examples.en: I transferred money to my friend.
I will transfer the salary into the account tomorrow.
If you transfer with the app, there is no fee.

examples.ko: 이체하기 전에 계좌 번호를 한 번 더 확인했어요.
examples.en: I checked the account number once more before transferring.

examples.ko: 방금 보험료를 이체해서 확인 문자가 왔어요.
examples.en: I just transferred the insurance payment and got a confirmation text.
Where should I transfer it?

explain: '이체하다'는 계좌에서 계좌로 돈을 옮기는 것이에요. 은행 앱에는 '이체하기' 버튼이 많고, 말할 때는 '송금하다'나 '보내다'도 자주 써요. 돈을 받는 곳은 현금이 아니라 '계좌'예요.
explain_en: 이체하다 means moving money from one account to another. Bank apps often have a button labeled 이체하기, and in speech people also say 송금하다 or 보내다. The money goes to an account, not to cash in hand.

examples.en: There is one small clinic in the village.

examples.ko: 진료소는 오후 다섯 시에 문을 닫아요.
examples.en: The clinic closes at five in the afternoon.
I caught a cold and went to the clinic.

examples.ko: 섬에는 큰 병원 대신 진료소만 있어요.
examples.en: On the island there is only a clinic instead of a big hospital.
The clinic prescribed me medicine.
They set up a temporary clinic in front of the event site.

explain: '진료소'는 작은 규모로 환자를 보는 곳이에요. 보통 '병원'보다 작고 시골 마을이나 행사장, 공항에 있어요. 도시에서 흔히 가는 곳은 '의원'이나 '병원'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 진료소 is a small place that sees patients. It is usually smaller than a 병원 and is found in rural villages, event sites, or airports. In cities, the places people usually visit are called 의원 or 병원.

en: brim; bill; visor (of a cap or hat)

examples.en: The brim of the hat blocks the sunlight.
I bought a wide-brimmed hat.
The hat brim got bent by the wind.
He pulled the visor down over his eyes.
I wrote my name on the brim of my baseball cap.

examples.ko: 챙 없는 모자는 햇볕에 얼굴이 타요.
examples.en: With a hat that has no brim, your face gets sunburned.

explain: '챙'은 모자 앞이나 둘레에 튀어나온 부분이에요. 야구 모자는 앞쪽에만 있고, 밀짚모자는 둘레에 둥글게 있어요. 소리가 비슷한 '챙기다'는 준비해서 가져간다는 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: 챙 is the part of a hat that sticks out at the front or all the way around. A baseball cap has it only at the front, while a straw hat has a round one. The similar-sounding 챙기다 is a different word meaning to get something ready and take it along.

examples.en: Please tell me the spelling of this word.
English spelling is difficult.
I got the spelling wrong and lost points.
Dictation is good for practicing spelling.
Please check if the spelling of the name is correct.
I found the typos with the spell check function.

explain: '철자'는 글자를 어떻게 쓰는지를 말해요. 한국어에서는 '맞춤법'을 더 자주 쓰는데, 맞춤법은 쓰는 규칙 전체이고 철자는 한 단어를 어떻게 쓰는지에 가까워요. '철자가 틀리다', '철자를 맞게 쓰다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: 철자 is how a word is spelled. Korean more often uses 맞춤법, which is the whole set of writing rules, while 철자 is closer to how one specific word is written. You say 철자가 틀리다 or 철자를 맞게 쓰다.

examples.en: The new president's inauguration is held tomorrow.
Many guests came to the inauguration.
I watched the inauguration on TV.
The inauguration took about an hour.
The principal gave a speech at the inauguration.
On the day of the inauguration, I received a bouquet.

explain: '취임식'은 새 대통령, 사장, 교장 같은 사람이 일을 시작하는 날 하는 행사예요. 일을 끝내고 떠날 때 하는 행사는 '퇴임식'이에요. 학교에서는 '입학식'과 '졸업식'이 짝이 되는 것처럼 '취임식'과 '퇴임식'도 짝이에요.
explain_en: 취임식 is the ceremony held when a new president, CEO, or principal starts their job. The ceremony for leaving a post is 퇴임식. Just as 입학식 and 졸업식 are a pair at school, 취임식 and 퇴임식 are a pair.

examples.en: We rode a canoe on the lake.

examples.ko: 카누는 두 사람이 함께 노를 저어요.
examples.en: Two people paddle a canoe together.

examples.ko: 주말에 카누 체험을 해 볼 거예요.
examples.en: I will try canoeing this weekend.

examples.ko: 강에 카누가 한 척 떠 있어요.
examples.en: A canoe is floating on the river.
Canoe racing is an Olympic event.
The child waved from the canoe.

explain: '카누'는 노를 저어서 움직이는 작고 좁은 배예요. 같은 노를 쓰는 '보트'는 더 넓고, 한국에서는 '배'가 가장 일반적인 말이에요. 배를 타는 것은 '타다'를 써서 '카누를 타다'라고 해요.
explain_en: 카누 is a small, narrow boat moved by paddling. A 보트 is wider, and 배 is the most general Korean word for a boat. You ride it with 타다, as in 카누를 타다.

examples.en: I think privacy is important.
Please respect other people's privacy.
If a room has no door, there is no privacy.
That article invaded the celebrity's privacy.

examples.ko: 프라이버시 때문에 사진은 올릴 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't post photos because of privacy.
Please check your privacy settings.

explain: '프라이버시'는 남이 모르게 하고 싶은 개인 생활이에요. 보통 '프라이버시를 지키다', '프라이버시를 침해하다'처럼 말해요. 한국어로 '사생활'이라고도 하는데, 일상에서는 '사생활'이 더 자연스러운 때가 많아요.
explain_en: 프라이버시 is the part of personal life that you want to keep away from others. People say 프라이버시를 지키다 or 프라이버시를 침해하다. The Korean word 사생활 means the same thing, and in daily speech it often sounds more natural.

examples.en: Grandfather sometimes talks to himself.
When I study, talking to myself helps me focus.
He talked to himself while walking down the street.
I can hear that person talking to themselves.
My little brother is talking to himself in his room.
What are you muttering to yourself like that?

explain: 듣는 사람 없이 혼자 말할 때 써요. 작게 중얼거리는 소리는 '중얼거리다', 입 안에서 웅얼거리는 소리는 '웅얼거리다'라고 해서 모양이 달라요. 보통은 명사 '혼잣말'을 써서 '혼잣말을 하다'라고 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when someone talks with no listener. Quiet muttering is '중얼거리다' and mumbling inside the mouth is '웅얼거리다', so the picture differs. People more often use the noun '혼잣말' and say '혼잣말을 하다'.

examples.en: The new car got a scratch.
This plate is cheap because it has a blemish.
I found a small scratch on the bag.
I picked only the fruit without blemishes.

examples.ko: 핸드폰 화면에 흠집이 생기지 않게 필름을 붙였어요.
examples.en: I put a film on the phone screen so it won't get scratched.
The scratch didn't come off even when I wiped it.

explain: '흠집'은 물건 겉에 생긴 작은 긁힘이나 상처예요. 사람의 몸에 난 것은 '상처'라고 해서 구분해요. '흠'만 쓰기도 하는데, '흠이 있다'는 사람이나 일의 단점이라는 뜻으로도 써요.

phrases.example: 나쁜 소문이 그 가게의 이름에 흠집을 냈어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건뿐 아니라 사람이나 회사의 이름, 평판을 나쁘게 만들 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used not only for objects but also for damaging a person's or company's name or reputation.

explain_en: 흠집 is a small scratch or mark on the surface of an object. A mark on a person's body is called 상처, so the two are kept apart. Sometimes just 흠 is used, and 흠이 있다 can also mean a person or thing has a fault.

en: adaptation (of a novel, etc. for film or stage)

examples.en: This drama is an adaptation of a novel.

examples.ko: 각색 때문에 원작과 이야기가 조금 달라요.
examples.en: Because of the adaptation, the story differs a bit from the original.
The director took charge of the adaptation himself.

examples.ko: 각색이 잘된 영화는 원작을 몰라도 재미있어요.
examples.en: A well-adapted film is fun even if you don't know the original.
They plan to adapt the webtoon into a drama.
That writer has a lot of adaptation experience.

explain: '각색'은 소설이나 만화를 영화, 드라마, 연극 대본으로 바꾸는 일이에요. 보통 '각색하다', '각색을 맡다'처럼 써요. 원래 이야기는 '원작'이라고 하고, 새로 처음부터 쓰는 것은 '창작'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 각색 is turning a novel or comic into a script for a film, drama, or play. It is used as 각색하다 or 각색을 맡다. The original story is the 원작, while writing something fully new is 창작.

examples.en: Rainfall is expected tonight.
There was little rainfall this year, so water is short.
The weather agency announced a regional rainfall forecast.
The baseball game was canceled because of rain.
A lot of rainfall was recorded in the mountains.
When the rain stops, the road will dry.

explain: '강우'는 비가 내리는 것을 날씨 뉴스에서 부르는 말이에요. 평소에는 그냥 '비'라고 하고, 비가 온 양은 '강우량'이라고 해요. 눈이 오는 것은 '강설', 비와 눈을 합쳐서는 '강수'라고 해요.
explain_en: 강우 is the word weather reports use for rain falling. In daily life people just say 비, and the amount of rain is 강우량. Snowfall is 강설, and rain and snow together are called 강수.

en: be going strong; be still doing well

examples.en: Grandfather is over eighty but is still going strong.
That singer is still going strong today.
I was glad the old shop was still doing well.

examples.ko: 우리 팀의 실력은 건재하다는 것을 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: We showed that our team's skill is still strong.
He appeared on stage looking as strong as ever.
The building stood firm even after the big accident.

explain: '건재하다'는 나이나 어려움이 있어도 힘이나 실력이 변하지 않았다고 말할 때 써요. 그냥 '건강하다'보다 '아직도 여전하다'는 느낌이 강해요. 사람뿐 아니라 가게, 건물, 팀에도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: 건재하다 is used to say that strength or skill hasn't changed despite age or hardship. It has a stronger sense of still being the same as before than plain 건강하다. It works for people but also for shops, buildings, and teams.

examples.en: I'm a scaredy-cat who is afraid of bugs.

examples.ko: 친구들이 놀이기구를 못 타는 저를 겁쟁이라고 놀렸어요.
examples.en: My friends teased me as a scaredy-cat for not riding the rides.
Even a coward has moments of courage.
That timid puppy hid at the sound of thunder.
Don't run away like a coward, try speaking up.
He isn't a coward, he's a careful person.

explain: '겁쟁이'는 무서움이 많은 사람을 장난스럽게나 놀리듯이 부르는 말이에요. 심하게 말하면 기분이 나쁠 수 있어서 친한 사이에서만 써요. 비슷한 '겁이 많다'는 설명하는 말이고, 부르는 말은 아니에요.
explain_en: 겁쟁이 is a playful or teasing name for someone who gets scared easily. It can hurt if said harshly, so it is used between close people. The similar 겁이 많다 is a description, not a name you call someone.

examples.en: An economist appeared on the news and explained prices.
My uncle is an economist who works at a university.
Economists carefully predict next year's economy.
I want to become an economist someday.

examples.ko: 경제학자의 책을 읽고 돈에 대해 많이 배웠어요.
examples.en: I read an economist's book and learned a lot about money.
Each economist thinks differently about this opinion.

explain: '경제학자'는 경제를 연구하는 학자예요. 은행이나 회사에서 시장을 살피는 사람은 '이코노미스트'나 '분석가'라고 부르기도 해요. 뉴스에서 '유명 경제학자'처럼 이름 앞에 자주 붙어요.
explain_en: 경제학자 is a scholar who studies the economy. People who watch markets at banks or companies are sometimes called 이코노미스트 or 분석가. On the news you often see it before a name, as in 유명 경제학자.

en: since it's already so; as long as

examples.en: Since you're already here, have a meal before you go.

examples.ko: 기왕 할 거면 제대로 해 보세요.
examples.en: If you're going to do it anyway, do it properly.

examples.ko: 기왕 사는 김에 하나 더 샀어요.
examples.en: Since I was buying one anyway, I bought one more.
Since I've already started, I'll see it through.
Since it turned out this way, let's laugh it off.

examples.ko: 기왕 가는 길에 우체국에 들러 줘요.
examples.en: Since you're going that way anyway, please stop by the post office.

explain: '기왕'은 이미 그렇게 된 상황에서 '그럴 바에는'이라고 말할 때 써요. 보통 뒤에 '-(으)니', '-(으)ㄹ 거면'이 와요. 같은 뜻으로 '이왕'도 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 방법 중 더 나은 쪽을 고를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to pick the better option when several choices are possible.

explain_en: 기왕 is used when something has already happened or been decided and you say "so we might as well". It usually goes with endings like -(으)니 or -(으)ㄹ 거면. 이왕 is also used with the same meaning.

en: a point on the way; chokepoint; corner of a road

examples.en: I waited for my friend at the corner in front of my house.
There is a bakery on the way to the market.
Cars were jammed at the narrow passage.
As we enter the start of winter, the weather turns chilly.
If you pass that spot, you can see the sea.
People stood at every corner and watched.

explain: '길목'은 길이 꺾이거나 어디론가 들어가는 중요한 지점이에요. '골목'은 집들 사이의 좁은 길이라서 달라요. '여름의 길목', '봄의 길목'처럼 계절이 바뀌는 때를 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: 길목 is an important point where a road bends or leads into somewhere. 골목 is a narrow lane between houses, so it is different. It can also mean the time when seasons change, as in 여름의 길목 or 봄의 길목.

examples.en: For dinner today we grilled and ate sea bream.
The sea bream is fresh, so it's popular at the raw fish restaurant.
I bought one sea bream at the market.
Sea bream has soft flesh and a clean taste.
My father caught sea bream while fishing.
Steamed sea bream often shows up on feast tables.

explain: '도미'는 몸이 납작하고 붉은빛이 도는 바닷물고기예요. 한국에서는 회나 구이, 찜으로 먹고 잔칫날에 올리는 고급 생선이에요. 생선 이름 뒤에 '회', '구이', '찜'을 붙여서 '도미회', '도미찜'처럼 요리 이름을 만들어요.
explain_en: 도미 is a flat, reddish-tinted sea fish. In Korea it is eaten as raw fish, grilled, or steamed, and it is a high-quality fish served on feast days. Adding 회, 구이, or 찜 gives dish names like 도미회 and 도미찜.

examples.en: In math, infinity is a size that has no end.
I drew the infinity symbol in my notebook.
The universe feels infinitely wide.
If you keep adding numbers, it approaches infinity.

examples.ko: 계산기에서 0으로 나누면 무한대가 아니라 오류가 나와요.
examples.en: If you divide by zero on a calculator, you get an error, not infinity.
That child has endless imagination.

explain: '무한대'는 수학에서 끝없이 커지는 크기를 말해요. 일상에서는 '무한'이나 '무제한'을 쓰기도 하는데, '무제한'은 '제한이 없다'는 뜻으로 요금제나 이용 규칙에 많이 나와요. '상상력이 무한대'처럼 한도가 없다는 과장으로도 써요.
explain_en: 무한대 is a quantity in math that grows without end. In daily life 무한 or 무제한 are also used, and 무제한 (no limit) is common for plans and rules. It is also used as an exaggeration for having no limit, as in 상상력이 무한대.

examples.ko: 이 병원은 민영이라서 비용이 조금 달라요.
examples.en: This hospital is privately run, so costs differ a bit.

examples.ko: 정부는 철도를 민영으로 바꾸지 않기로 했어요.
examples.en: The government decided not to make the railway private.

examples.ko: 민영 방송과 공영 방송은 운영 방식이 달라요.
examples.en: Private and public broadcasters are run in different ways.
This is a road that private buses run on.

examples.ko: 민영 보험은 가입하는 사람이 직접 선택해요.
examples.en: People choose private insurance for themselves.
I want to work at a private company.

explain: '민영'은 나라가 아니라 회사나 개인이 운영하는 것이에요. 반대말은 나라가 운영하는 '국영'이에요. '민영 방송', '민영 기업'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙여서 많이 써요.
explain_en: 민영 means run by a company or an individual, not by the state. The opposite is 국영, run by the state. It is mostly attached in front of other nouns, as in 민영 방송 or 민영 기업.

examples.en: The scent of white lilies fills the room.
The bride is holding a bouquet of lilies.
Lilies bloom big in summer.
Mother planted lilies in the garden.
I bought two lilies at the flower shop.
The lilies were so fragrant that I got a headache.

explain: '백합'은 크고 하얀 꽃이 피고 향기가 진한 꽃이에요. 결혼식이나 장례식 꽃으로 자주 쓰여요. 꽃을 셀 때는 '송이'를 써서 '백합 한 송이'라고 해요.
explain_en: 백합 is a lily with large white flowers and a strong scent. It is often used for wedding or funeral flowers. Flowers are counted with 송이, as in 백합 한 송이.

examples.en: My father is a collector who gathers old coins.
The collector bought a rare stamp at a high price.

examples.ko: 저는 인형 수집가라서 집에 인형이 많아요.
examples.en: I'm a doll collector, so I have lots of dolls at home.
That collector's room is full of books.
The museum borrowed paintings from a collector.
Art collectors often visit exhibitions.

explain: 우표·동전·그림처럼 한 가지를 오래, 진지하게 모으는 사람에게 써요. 가볍게 모으는 사람은 그냥 '모으는 사람'이라고 해요. '우표 수집가'처럼 앞에 모으는 물건을 붙이고, 같은 뜻으로 '컬렉터'도 써요.
explain_en: It is used for someone who seriously collects one kind of thing over a long time, such as stamps, coins or paintings. Someone who collects casually is just called '모으는 사람'. You put the collected item in front, as in '우표 수집가', and '컬렉터' is also used with the same meaning.

examples.en: I learn sign language every weekend.
Sign language communicates with hands and facial expressions.

examples.ko: 뉴스 화면 한쪽에서 수화 통역을 해 줘요.
examples.en: Sign language interpretation is shown on one side of the news screen.
That friend talks in sign language.
I want to join a sign language club.
The sign language teacher showed it slowly.

explain: '수화'는 손 모양과 움직임으로 말하는 언어예요. 요즘은 '수어'라는 말을 더 많이 권장하고, 한국어의 소리와 다른 독립된 언어라는 뜻을 담아요. 둘 다 쓰이니 뉴스나 학교에서는 '한국 수어'도 알아 두세요.
explain_en: 수화 is a language spoken with hand shapes and movements. These days 수어 is more often recommended, stressing that it is a language separate from spoken Korean. Both are used, so also learn 한국 수어, which you will see in news and schools.

examples.ko: 우리 팀 스트라이커가 두 골을 넣었어요.
examples.en: Our team's striker scored two goals.
I played striker in the game.
A striker receives the ball close to the goal.
That player is famous as a fast striker.
The coach picked a new striker.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 스트라이커가 되는 게 꿈이었어요.
examples.en: Since I was little, my dream was to be a striker.

explain: '스트라이커'는 축구에서 앞쪽에서 골을 넣는 일을 주로 하는 선수예요. 한국어로는 '공격수'라고도 해서, '공격수'가 더 넓게 앞쪽 선수를 가리켜요. 수비를 맡는 선수는 '수비수', 골문을 지키는 선수는 '골키퍼'라고 해요.
explain_en: 스트라이커 is a soccer player whose main job is scoring goals up front. The Korean word 공격수 covers attacking players more broadly. A player who defends is a 수비수, and the one guarding the goal is a 골키퍼.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 빠른 역습으로 골을 넣었어요.
examples.en: Our team scored with a fast counterattack.
We must watch out for the other team's counterattack.
When the counterattack began, the crowd stood up.
After defending, they went straight into a counterattack.
The coach made them practice the counterattack a lot.

examples.ko: 체스에서 상대의 실수를 틈타 역습에 성공했어요.
examples.en: In chess, I took advantage of my opponent's mistake and pulled off a counterattack.

explain: '역습'은 공격을 받다가 갑자기 반대로 공격하는 것이에요. 축구에서 가장 많이 쓰고, 말싸움이나 경기에서 뒤집을 때도 써요. 비슷한 '반격'은 더 넓게 쓰이고, 역습은 빠르게 뒤집는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: 역습 is suddenly turning around to attack after being attacked. It is used most in soccer, and also for turning an argument or game around. The similar 반격 is broader, while 역습 has a stronger feeling of a quick reversal.

examples.en: I put wax in my hair.

examples.ko: 왁스를 너무 많이 쓰면 머리가 무거워요.
examples.en: If you use too much wax, your hair feels heavy.

examples.ko: 저는 매일 아침 왁스로 머리를 세워요.
examples.en: Every morning I style my hair upright with wax.
When I applied wax to the floor, it shone.
When you wax a car, the rainwater runs off.
This wax has a nice smell.

explain: 한국에서 '왁스'라고 하면 먼저 머리 스타일을 만드는 '헤어 왁스'를 떠올려요. 바닥이나 자동차에 바르는 왁스는 앞에 말을 붙여서 '마루 왁스', '자동차 왁스'처럼 구분해요. 머리에 바르는 것은 '왁스를 바르다'라고 해요.
explain_en: In Korea 왁스 first brings to mind 헤어 왁스, used to style hair. Wax for floors or cars is told apart by adding a word in front, like 마루 왁스 or 자동차 왁스. For hair you say 왁스를 바르다.

examples.en: Work was very busy in the first half of this year.
The first-half results were better than the second half.
That team came first in the first half of the season.
First-semester classes begin in March.
The boss announced the first-half plan.
When the first half ends, there is a break.

explain: '전반기'는 일 년이나 한 시즌을 둘로 나눌 때 앞쪽 반이에요. 뒤쪽 반은 '후반기'라고 해요. 축구나 농구 경기의 앞쪽 반은 보통 '전반'이라고 하고, 일 년이나 학기, 야구 시즌처럼 긴 기간에는 '전반기'를 써요.
explain_en: 전반기 is the first half when a year or a season is split in two. The second half is 후반기. For the first half of a soccer or basketball game people usually say 전반, while 전반기 is used for long periods like a year, a semester, or a baseball season.
